entry.title: Release history
entry.summary: Every DocKitty toolkit release, rendered at build time from the repository's CHANGELOG.md.
entry.content:
All notable changes to @spec-kitty/doc-toolkit are recorded here. The format follows Keep a Changelog, and the project adheres to Semantic Versioning.

Unreleased

💥 Breaking

  • dockitty-assert-plantuml-no-remote-include --service-container now fails service setups it used to pass (#268). Before, the check passed any service that refused its test include. Now, with the opt-in unset, it fails when the named container has: a PLANTUML_SECURITY_PROFILE that is missing or not SANDBOX; a security-relevant -D property, plantuml.* env key or PLANTUML_PROPERTY_FILE; a Java @argfile; or a local --server port the container does not publish on a matching address. An empty value for any flag now exits 2. To fix: set PLANTUML_SECURITY_PROFILE=SANDBOX on the service (or declare the opt-in), move PlantUML settings into the two environment variables, and name the container that serves --server. See the 0.6 to 0.7 migration guide.

Added

  • Operators can let PlantUML fetch declared remote includes (#268). Before, every URL include failed the build under the hardened SANDBOX service. Now plantumlAllowExternal (or DK_PLANTUML_ALLOW_EXTERNAL) accepts exactly three values: unset (sandbox, the default, unchanged), a list of URL prefixes (allowlist mode), or internet. The build prints the declared entries, and dockitty-assert-plantuml-no-remote-include verifies that the running service matches them. An entry must end in / and may not carry :80/ or :443/. Most sites need no change: bundled <C4/...> includes work in the default sandbox. See ADR-0074 and Allowing external includes.

  • Any MCP client can read a DocKitty site’s published artifacts (#284). Before, an agent had to fetch and stitch /api/index.json and /api/pages/*.json itself. Now the new @spec-kitty/doc-kitty-mcp workspace package serves them over stdio: run pnpm pack --filter @spec-kitty/doc-kitty-mcp, install the tarball, and launch doc-kitty-mcp --site <url> or --dir <dist>. Registry publishing is deferred, so the tarball is the supported form. Every site’s /api/*.json also gains buildId (to detect a torn read) and, on the index, sections. A site that sets links: { mcp: true } advertises the wiring in _links.mcp and llms.txt. See ADR-0073 and the MCP server quickstart.

  • The footer links the site’s machine entry points on every page. Before, an agent had to know the paths of llms.txt, the agent API and the rest. Now a Machine-readable group lists each one the site serves, with or without a theme, and never one it doesn’t. Set footer: { machineEntryPoints: false } to remove the group, or { label: '...' } to rename it. The <head> RSS and llms.txt links follow what the site serves too, so a site with no rss.xml route no longer advertises one. A site that sets starlight.head now gets these links too, where its entries used to replace the toolkit’s head; if it added its own RSS alternate, the page now has two.

  • A group’s title can be the link to its index page (#290). Set sidebar: { titleIsIndex: true } and a generated sidebar group’s label links to its index page, with no “Overview” entry below it, and a separate chevron opens and closes the group. A group with no index page keeps its plain toggle, and previous and next links are unchanged. The option is off by default, and with it off Starlight’s own sidebar renders as before. It cannot be set together with sidebar.indexLabel. A sidebar you write yourself is not changed.

  • Every published, dated page gets an Atom entry at /api/pages/<id>.atom.xml. Before, a page had only a JSON record. Now the toolkit injects the route on every site, with nothing to mount, and builds a deterministic Atom entry document with the page’s rendered HTML. A draft or a page with no updated or generated.at date gets none. Set pageFormats: { atom: false } to turn it off. A static host picks the response Content-Type from the .xml extension, so type=entry is guaranteed only in the link that points at the entry. A site with no site gets no entries and no Atom links, with one build warning, because an Atom id must be a stable absolute IRI. An .mdx page’s entry has no <content>, a local image becomes its alt text, and characters XML 1.0 forbids are removed from Atom and RSS output. The id changes when the domain, base or slug changes.

  • Each published page links its JSON, OKF and Atom versions, in the footer and the <head>. A draft, a page outside the docs collection, or a page with agent: { discoverable: false } has none: that opt-out also hides the links (its source link stays, as that is for reading the file). Only the links go: the page’s JSON, Atom and OKF files are still built and served. Set repository: { provider, repo, branch, siteDir } to add a source link to the page’s file on GitHub, GitLab or Bitbucket; a generated page has none, and self-hosted instances are not supported. The links are pills under the spec-kitty theme and plain links without it.

  • Pages and sections can show an icon in the sidebar (#293). Set sidebar.icon on a page, or icon on a section in sections.yaml or a charter’s sections.entries, to fa-<name> for Font Awesome’s solid set or to the name of a Starlight built-in. A group takes its section’s icon, or else its index page’s. Only the icons you use reach the output, as inline SVG hidden from assistive technology, with no font file and no external request, and a page showing a Font Awesome icon carries one CC BY 4.0 licence comment. An unknown name fails the build and validate-frontmatter, naming the page or section. A site with no icons is unchanged. A sidebar you write yourself takes no icons, and the build warns once if any are authored.

Changed

  • Metadata blocks start collapsed (#290). Before, Who is this for, Related, External references and Glossary links used always showed in full, and on a page with several they pushed the content down. Now each starts closed behind a control with its label and count, such as “Related (3)”. They open by mouse or keyboard, also with scripts off, start closed again on the next page, print open, and stay in search. Set metadataBlocks: { collapsed: false } to keep them open. See ADR-0077.

  • Generated sidebar groups start closed (#290). Before, the groups of the generated sidebar were open on every page, apart from any a site had set to collapse, such as the generated API groups. Now each starts closed, except the groups on the path to the current page, which Starlight opens by itself. Set sidebar: { collapsed: false } to keep the old sidebar exactly. A sidebar you write yourself is not changed.

Fixed

  • The agent index no longer names a surface the site does not mount (#290). Before, /api/index.json linked rss, bibliography, scenarios, llms and sitemap, and each record’s self, unless the site turned the first four off through links, so a site without one of those routes shipped a dangling link. Now the toolkit detects the surfaces from the site’s routes at their standard paths, and _links follows that. llms follows the llms.txt route, and sitemap needs both the sitemap and site to be set, so a build with no site has no sitemap link. IndexLinks.llms and IndexLinks.sitemap are now optional in the contract types. An explicit links value still wins for rss, bibliography, scenarios and pages, which is how to link a route at another path; llms and sitemap have no override.

0.6.0 — 2026-11-02

Added

  • A site can publish versioned API reference pages from its OpenAPI files (#244). Before, DocKitty had no API reference: authors linked to a separate Swagger site or pasted the spec into a page. Now an openapi option in defineDocKittyIntegrations takes OpenAPI 3.0 or 3.1 files, each with a label and released flag, and builds reference pages at /reference/api/<label>/ inside the normal frame, with version links and an “unreleased” badge. Each version also publishes its raw file, byte for byte, and an openapi.<ext>.sha256 that sha256sum -c checks, and gets a line in llms.txt. The option is off by default and needs two optional peers, starlight-openapi@0.27.0 and @astrojs/markdown-satteri@0.4.4. A bad path, file or label fails the build with a [dk-openapi] error. A strict CSP needs one script hash and one style-attribute hash (with 'unsafe-hashes'). See Publish OpenAPI reference pages and ADR-0049.

  • A kind: Schematic page documents a JSON or YAML schema (#245). Before, a schema stayed a file that readers opened in a repository. Now a page with kind: Schematic and schematic_path: <file> (relative to the project root, inside it) keeps your own Markdown as the body. The toolkit adds the schema description before it, then ## Diagram, ## Properties and ## Source; a ## heading you write with one of those names replaces the generated one. $ref within the file or to another file in the root is followed, and a URL $ref renders as a link. A bad path, a parse error, a non-schema file or an unresolvable $ref fails the build with a [dk-schematic] error. The diagram needs build-mode diagrams and the PlantUML service, so client mode leaves it out. The schema is published unchanged beside the page, and the OKF export resource points at it. No new option; yaml is a new dependency. See ADR-0067.

  • A site can leave whole docs folders out of the build (#247). Before, the docs loader refused any pattern but the default, so a folder you keep in git but do not publish (an archive, internal reports, working notes) was built, schema-checked and link-checked like any other. Now defineDocKittyIntegrations({ exclude: ['archive', 'plans/engineering-notes'] }) leaves those folders out of the loader, the routes, the sidebar, search, the sitemap, rss.xml, llms.txt, the agent API and the ADR Hub, and validate-frontmatter and check-links --strict skip them. Entries are folder paths relative to docsDir, with no globs, and each must exist with the same letter case. A link or related: ref from a published page into an excluded folder is reported as “target is excluded from the site”; assert-no-broken-links and generate-adr-index take a new --docs <dir> option to read the list. Without exclude nothing changes. See ADR-0070.

  • Date-named ADRs get real ids, order and status (#248). Before, an ADR’s id was always its leading four digits, so 2026-03-09-1-slug.md read as 2026. Its status came only from a body ## Status section, and its date only from updated. Now a docs tree can set adr.id in docs/_meta/charter.yaml: preset: date-seq reads 2026-03-09-1 and orders by date, then by sequence number (-2 before -10), and pattern: takes a regex with a named id group. When an ADR has no body ## Status, its frontmatter status is shown, and when it has no updated, its frontmatter date. The generated ADR index and the hub’s ADR cards still share one extractor. Without the axis nothing changes. generate-adr-index.mjs reads the charter next to --dir, or the one under the new --docs-root. See ADR-0069.

  • Old .html URLs keep working after a move from DocFX (#249). Before, an Astro redirect keyed on /a/b.html was written as the folder dist/a/b.html/index.html, which a static host does not serve at /a/b.html. A key /a/b/index.html replaced the live page /a/b/ with a folder, and the redirect-coverage gate could not check .html URLs at all. Now the legacyHtmlRedirects option of defineDocKittyIntegrations ({ '/a/b.html': '/a/b/' }, without the base) writes a flat dist/a/b.html stub after the build. The stub is noindex, has a canonical link to the target, and is not in the sitemap, llms.txt or the agent API. It works at the domain root and under a base path, and chains in the map are shortened to one step. The gate looks up a baselined .html URL as that file, follows chains, and fails on a missing stub or a dead target. --declared-redirects may now be repeated. The new dockitty-generate-legacy-redirects command writes the mechanical map (x.html -> x/, x/index.html -> x/) from a committed list of old URLs. See ADR-0071 and Keeping .html URLs.

  • GitHub alert blockquotes render as Starlight asides (#250). Before, a > [!NOTE] blockquote rendered as a plain quote that started with a literal [!NOTE], and converting it to :::note broke the page on GitHub. Now, with the new githubAlerts: true option, a top-level blockquote that opens with [!NOTE], [!TIP], [!IMPORTANT], [!WARNING] or [!CAUTION] renders as the matching native aside: note, tip, note titled “Important”, caution titled “Warning” and danger titled “Caution”. They share the theme and accessible name of :::note and the Markua callouts. A plain quote, an unknown [!X] marker and a deck page are unchanged. Off by default, so existing sites render as before. See ADR-0068.

  • The link and frontmatter checks can leave a folder out. Before, a folder of files that are not pages, such as changelog fragments in a repository’s own docs/, could only be left out through a built site’s exclude option. Now dockitty-check-links and dockitty-validate-frontmatter take --exclude <folder>, once per folder. The folder must exist inside one of the roots, or the command exits with status 2. See ADR-0072.

Changed

  • An Astro redirects key that ends in .html fails a static build (#249). Before, it built a folder that a static host does not serve at that URL, or replaced a live page. Now a static build (output: 'static' with build.redirects on) stops and names each key. Move those entries to legacyHtmlRedirects, without the base on the target. A server-output (adapter) site, or one whose adapter sets build.redirects: false, keeps its .html keys: Astro writes no files for them, and the adapter (or Astro at request time) answers them. A key that is also a legacyHtmlRedirects source fails in every mode.

  • An adr.id pattern may be written in upper case (#271). Before, pattern: '^(?<id>ADR-\d+)-' matched no ADR, because the pattern runs against the lowercased file name, and then (#269, never released) failed at charter load. Now such a pattern is matched case-insensitively, so it reads ADR-12-Use-X.md on the hub and in the generated index alike. The id shows lowercased (adr-12), so it agrees with the page’s URL. Escapes such as \D and \W, group names and back-references keep their meaning. A lower-case pattern compiles exactly as before. See the amendment note in ADR-0069.

  • The ADR index is regenerated after merge, not in each PR. Before, every PR that added an ADR also added a row to the table in docs/adr/README.md, and CI failed a stale table, so parallel PRs conflicted on it. Now a bot PR regenerates the table after merge, and CI checks per PR only that no two ADRs share a number, with the new generate-adr-index.mjs --check-ids. See ADR-0072.

  • Changelog entries are fragment files. Before, every PR added its entry to the one [Unreleased] section of CHANGELOG.md, so parallel PRs conflicted on the same lines. Now a PR adds one file under docs/changelog/unreleased/, and pnpm changelog:release <version> writes the fragments into the version section at release time. Released history is unchanged. The example site shows pending fragments as Unreleased. See ADR-0072.

  • A large JSON diagram stays at the size PlantUML drew it, and selecting it opens the same drawing centered at full size.

  • CI is ready for a merge queue, and a PR can pause its CI. Before, CI ran only on pull requests and pushes, so a merge queue would have waited forever for ci-ok. Now ci.yml also runs on merge_group, and a PR labelled pr:pause-ci skips every lane with ci-ok red until the label goes. The CI helper tests run in CI, and a change to .github/scripts, .github/actions or .github/filters.yml runs every lane. See ADR-0072.

Security

  • The PlantUML render service is pinned by digest and refuses remote includes (#251). Before, every workflow ran the floating plantuml/plantuml-server:jetty tag, so a re-tag silently changed the renderer. The server also ran with its default INTERNET profile, so a diagram with !includeurl (or an !include of a URL) was fetched at build time. Now ci.yml, deploy.yml and update-a11y-baselines.yml run jetty-v1.2026.9@sha256:065c66ad… with PLANTUML_SECURITY_PROFILE=SANDBOX. Such a diagram renders as an error and fails the build. A new bin, dockitty-assert-plantuml-no-remote-include, proves this against a live service, and CI runs it before building: it serves a canary, checks that the canary is reachable from inside the service container, and requires the !includeurl and !include <url> fixtures to be refused with zero canary requests. The consumer guide now shows the hardened service block. To adopt it, copy that block; a diagram that includes a URL or a local file will then stop the build.

Documentation

  • The setup guide says how to write redirect targets for a site at the domain root (#261). Before, a config that built its Astro redirects targets as `${BASE}${to}` with BASE = '/' produced //new/, which a browser reads as a link to another host. The guide now says to use '' at the root or strip the trailing slash, and the example config strips it.

0.5.0 — 2026-10-25

💥 Breaking

  • validate-frontmatter requires kind on every page again (#219). Before, the gate accepted a page without kind (since #38), while the convention, ADR-0009 and the charter said it was required. Now a page without kind fails with `kind`: required, the bundle-root README.md included. The build still renders such a page, and an unknown kind value still only warns. To keep the old behaviour, list kind under required_fields.optional in docs/_meta/charter.yaml. See ADR-0065 and Upgrading from 0.4.0 to 0.5.0.

Changed

  • On screens wider than the frame, the sidebar tint now reaches the screen edge (#224). Before, above the 120rem default cap the sidebar panel’s tint started at the frame edge, so it looked like a block floating 320px in under a header that runs edge to edge. Now the panel’s tint runs out to the viewport’s start edge, as the header bar does, and its links stay on the frame. Nothing changes at or below 1920px, or on a full-width frame. Recorded in ADR-0066.

Fixed

  • The table of contents rail no longer jumps across the page on a slow first paint (#223). Before, if the browser painted before the reading pane was parsed, the rail (or, collapsed, its 1px line) was drawn next to the left sidebar and then jumped to its place, a layout shift of about 0.25. Now it is in its final place in every paint. Nothing moves once the page has loaded.
  • The collapsed reading column clears the rail toggle under any frame cap (#220). Before, a site that capped the frame between 72rem and 84rem and was viewed on a wider screen had the collapsed column run 7px under the toggle. The column’s end padding is now worked out from the width of the row the pane and rail share, not from the viewport. The default frame is unchanged.
  • The load-shift layout test no longer flakes (#222). It counted shifts from Starlight’s own markup still parsing in, and failed in about a quarter of runs under parallel load. It now paints the whole page first, then runs the enhancement and counts every shift, still requiring exactly 0, with a positive control that proves a real shift is caught. It runs against the published build again.
  • Agent page records now give an absolute source (#236). Before, on a site with a base, source was a site-relative path that returned a 404. Now it is absolute, includes the base, and equals _links.self.href and the source in the agent index.
  • OKF export links work on sites with a base (#237). Before, links between pages and links to site files lost the base or pointed one folder too deep. Now .md links resolve against the linking page and become bundle paths, and other site links carry <site><base>. --site-url takes the origin and the export adds the base. The advisory link check also reports unresolved relative links.
  • OKF export keeps the prose of section README files (#238). Before, the export dropped the body of a section README, so its text and links were missing from the bundle. Now a README with body text is written as a page at <id>.md, such as guides/README.md, with its links rewritten. The section index.md stays a strict OKF entry list and lists that page first. A README with no body exports as before.
  • Written-out and numeric dates read the same on every build machine (#234). Before, a non-ISO value with no zone, such as updated: May 1, 2024 or 1/2/24, was read in the build machine’s time zone, so the same source gave different instants, feed order and agent-API dates. In Pacific/Auckland, May 1, 2024 became 2024-04-30T12:00:00Z. Now it is read as UTC, like an ISO value with no zone, and so is a rolled-over one such as 2024-04-31T10:00. A value that names its zone (GMT, UTC, Z, EST, or +0200 after the time) keeps it. The gate still recommends YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ.
  • The example’s Cucumber report regenerates byte-identically (#231). Before, every regeneration of example/reports/cucumber.ndjson was a diff of hundreds of lines, from machine details, timestamps and random ids. Now src/scripts/normalise-cucumber-report.mjs fixes them: meta, timestamps (to a named --at instant), durations, ids, and the run directory in stack traces. PROVENANCE.txt ends the procedure with it, and a test fails if the committed report is not normalised.
  • Decision-index lock files are no longer tracked (#232). Seven older missions still tracked a transient kitty-specs/**/decisions/index.json.lock. They are removed from the index; the .gitignore rule keeps them out.

0.4.0 — 2026-10-19

This release moves the toolkit to Astro 7.4 and Starlight 0.42.6, and needs Node 22.22.0 or later. Pages render as they did on 0.3.0: heading anchor links stay off and the HTML keeps its whitespace. Readers get a full-window view for diagrams and images, a draft notice on draft pages, and a sidebar that no longer jumps. Authors get Gherkin authoring aids and a Specification layout for feature pages. Every build publishes a content graph and an OKF export bundle, and the agent API is now version 3. The page frame is capped at 120rem by default. The release removes what 0.3.0 deprecated, so committed generated pages must be regenerated once, and it rejects a date field that is not a date. Upgrading from 0.3.0: read the Breaking section and the 0.3 to 0.4 migration guide first.

💥 Breaking

  • Install Astro 7, Starlight 0.42 and @astrojs/markdown-remark 7, on Node 22.22.0 or later (#119, #144, #145, #146). Before, the toolkit needed Astro 5 and Starlight 0.32. Now its peer ranges are astro >=7.2.10 <8, @astrojs/starlight >=0.42.0 <0.43.0 and @astrojs/markdown-remark >=7.3.0 <8, and engines.node is >=22.22.0. Run pnpm add astro@^7.4.0 @astrojs/starlight@^0.42.6 @astrojs/markdown-remark@^7.3.3 and use Node 22.22 or later locally and in CI. The toolkit sets Astro’s Markdown processor to unified() itself (ADR-0060), so remark and rehype plugins you add through markdown.remarkPlugins / rehypePlugins keep working; do not set markdown.processor yourself. Astro 7 and Starlight 0.42 bring their own breaking changes for code you wrote outside the toolkit, such as your own components or pages; see their upgrade guides.
  • Build schema extensions on zod 4 via astro/zod: the exported docs schema (./schema) is now a zod 4 schema. Before, it was built on zod 3. Now it imports from astro/zod, and .default(...) becomes .prefault(...) semantics (the default is parsed through the schema, not returned as is). If you extend docKittyDocsSchema with your own fields, import z from astro/zod and write them for zod 4; a zod 3 schema no longer composes with it.
  • Read the producer from generated_by: api/scenarios.json no longer has generated_from, and its version is "2" (#183). Before, every record carried generated_from: "doc-kitty/gherkin" next to generated_by, with version: "1". Now generated_from is gone and version is "2"; nothing else in the record moved. Clients that read generated_from or pin version "1" need updating.
  • Regenerate committed Gherkin and glossary pages once: the 0.3.0 stamps now fail the frontmatter check (#210). Before, a page stamped with the unversioned generated.by: doc-kitty/gherkin or doc-kitty/glossary, or with a sha256: hash in generated.at, was still treated as generated. Now such a stamp is retired: the page is no longer exempt as a generated page, and dockitty-validate-frontmatter fails it with a message that names the regeneration step. Run dockitty-generate-feature-pages for Gherkin pages, and astro build (or astro dev) for glossary pages; both still own and overwrite pages with a retired stamp, and write the versioned <producer>/<version> stamp with content_hash. Commit the result.
  • Read updated as a full UTC timestamp in the agent API, now version 3 (#177). Before, api/index.json reported version: "2" and each page’s updated as a date such as 2026-10-18. Now it reports version: "3" and updated as 2026-10-18T00:00:00Z. Agents or scripts that pin the version or parse a date-only value need updating. Nothing else in the record moved.
  • Produce the Gherkin report before every CI docs build, or set gherkin.results.required: false (#166). Before, a missing gherkin.results report only logged a warning and the site built without results, so a CI job could publish a site with no results unnoticed. Now, when the CI environment variable holds anything other than empty, false or 0, a missing report stops the build and the message names the report and the opt-out. GitHub Actions sets CI=true in every job, so preview and docs-only jobs without a report are the ones that fail. Run Cucumber in the same job first, or download its report as an artifact. For jobs that never run the tests, set gherkin: { results: { report: 'reports/cucumber.ndjson', required: false } } and they warn as before. Local builds still warn only. An unreadable or malformed report fails as it did.
  • The page frame is capped at 120rem by default (#205). Before, the frame spanned the viewport unless a site set --dk-width-frame. Now the default is 120rem. Viewports of 1920px and narrower look as before. On a wider viewport the frame is 1920px wide and centred: at 2560px a rail page has 192px beside the column instead of 512px. To keep a full-width frame, set :root { --dk-width-frame: 100%; }. A site that already sets the token is unaffected. See Cap the page width and ADR-0064.
  • Write every date as a date, not a bare number or a short string: the build and the frontmatter gate now reject what they accepted before (#227). Before, the build took anything JavaScript’s Date could parse for updated, stale_after, generated.at and verified[].at, and the gate passed 1, "1", "2024" and 20241001 with a warning, so updated: 1 built and published a wrong date. Now a value must have a date shape and Date must read it: a YAML date, ISO-8601, YYYY-MM, a string with a month name and a number, or one with three or more numeric groups (the last three draw a nonIso advisory). Numbers, "1/2", "abc 2024", "2024.5" and 18/10/2026 fail, in both, with a message that names the field and YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ. A retired sha256: stamp in generated.at is also rejected by the build, where only the gate did before. To list every page in one pass, run dockitty-validate-frontmatter docs, then fix each, for example updated: 2024-10-01T00:00:00Z. See the ADR-0059 note.

Added

  • Readers can expand diagrams and images to the full window again (#185). Before, sites built on the toolkit drew diagrams and images at page width with no way to enlarge them; the older portal sites had a lightbox that the toolkit never carried over. Now every diagram has an expand button, and every image in page content expands on click or Enter. It opens in a modal that closes with Esc, the close button or a click outside, and focus returns to where it was. It is on for every site, with no option and no new dependency. Its labels are English only for now (#161).
  • Every build publishes api/content-graph.json (#176). Before, an agent or tool that wanted the site’s structure fetched one JSON file per page, and nothing held the reverse edges. Now one file lists every published page, persona, catalog entry and external resource, plus each frontmatter relation between them (related, audience, cites, in-section, derived-from). It is built by the same resolvers as the rendered blocks, sorted for identical bytes on every build, linked from api/index.json, and drafts stay out. The artifact gate fails on any edge that points nowhere.
  • Export a plain OKF v0.2 bundle (#178). Before, OKF readers saw a DocKitty site as unconnected pages, because they only follow body links. Now every build writes dist/okf/, and dockitty-export-okf writes the same bundle on demand. Relations become /-prefixed body links, links to pages point at bundle paths, index files take OKF form, and doc_status, updated and authors map to OKF status, generated and actors. A built-in checker (--check) verifies OKF §11. Drafts are left out.
  • Translate the sidebar “Overview” label, or set it once (#161). Before, the index entry of a nested group read “Overview” in English on every site. Now the word is the UI string dockitty.sidebar.indexLabel: translate it in your Starlight i18n files and each language shows its own word. To set one label for all languages, use defineDocKittyIntegrations({ sidebar: { indexLabel: 'Intro' } }); it wins over the translation. The sidebar option accepts either the Starlight sidebar array you may already pass or this { indexLabel } object; an unknown key or a blank label stops the build. Previous and next links keep the page title. With neither set, your sidebar is unchanged.
  • A stale report now says so on a single scenario (#166). Before, a ::gherkin{src=… scenario=…} include showed nothing when the report was made from another version of the file, so the missing result looked like a gap. Now its result line reads “Results not shown: the test report was made from a different version of this file.”
  • A hand-mounted scenarios route without results warns (#166). Before, a site with its own src/pages/api/scenarios.json route that called scenarioIndexRoute() without results served an index with no results and no sign why. Now, while gherkin.results is set, the build logs one warning per astro build and one per astro dev run, naming the route file and the value to pass.
  • Follow _links through the agent API instead of building URLs (#103). Before, api/index.json and the per-page records held no links, so an agent had to know the URL scheme. Now the index links to itself, llms.txt and the sitemap, plus the feed, bibliography and scenarios routes you mount. Each record links to its per-page JSON, its HTML page and its related pages, and a per-page record also links up to the index. The keys are additive; the index version is '3' because of the updated change (#177). The links option on agentIndexRoute and agentPageRoute defaults to all on, as in the worked example; pass false for a surface your site does not mount. If you mount the index elsewhere, pass indexPath to both routes, and keep it ending in /api/index.json. pnpm assert:artifacts now fails when a _links href in dist/api/ points at a file the build did not produce. See ADR-0058.
  • Point the build check at a moved agent index with --index-path (#172). Before, assert:artifacts read only dist/api/index.json, so a site that mounts the index elsewhere (indexPath: '/v2/api/index.json') could not run the check. Now assert:artifacts --index-path v2/api/index.json moves every index check to that file. The path is relative to dist (without the site base). The check takes the base from the index’s self link and follows _links to other JSON files wherever they sit. One leading / is ignored; a value containing .., an empty value, or a drive or // path exits 2. Without the flag, nothing changes.
  • Set a glossary context once per folder with gherkin.defaultGlossaryContext (#197). Before, a generated feature page got glossary_context only from a @dk:context tag on each feature. Now a map such as { shipping: 'shipping', 'shipping/eu': 'customs' } gives every page under a source folder its context. The longest matching folder wins, compared by whole folder name, and a feature’s own @dk:context tag still wins over it. The drift gate takes the same map as repeated --default-glossary-context <dir>=<context> flags. A key that matches no feature folder warns, and the site build warns about a context the glossary does not define (ADR-0061).
  • Turn on the imperative-step lint with gherkin.lint.imperativeSteps (#196). Before, nothing checked for steps such as When I click "#book-button". Now, when the option is on, the build warns about each Given or When step that names a UI action (click, tap, fill in, …) or quotes a CSS selector, on generated feature pages and in-page gherkin fences. It is off by default, never fails a build and never changes a page. verbs, extend and keywords adjust the phrase list and scope. Includes, gherkin raw fences and non-English features are not checked (ADR-0061).
  • Silence the imperative-step lint with @dk:allow=imperative (#196). The tag works on a Feature, a Rule or a Scenario, and is the first @dk: tag read below Feature level. Any other value warns (ADR-0061).
  • Feature pages show their tags and source in a header card (#198). The new base-kind Specification layout renders a labelled card above the scenarios. The source is a link when the site sets sourceUrlPrefix. The “On this page” list stays the scenario list, and the results summary stays in the body. A theme opts out by mapping layouts.Specification to Default.astro (ADR-0062).
  • Every draft page shows a draft notice (#198). Before, a draft page looked exactly like an active one. Now a draft page of any kind shows “Draft. This page is a work in progress and may change.” under its title when drafts are built. The site root is never shown as a draft, and out-of-frame slide decks are not covered (ADR-0062).
  • The current sidebar entry is revealed before first paint (#203). Before, the reveal ran from a head script after the page had loaded. Now Sidebar is the toolkit’s sixth carrier: it renders Starlight’s own sidebar unchanged and then the script that reveals the current entry. Like the other carriers, it replaces a Sidebar override passed through starlight.components. A Starlight plugin that overrides Sidebar still wins over the carrier, and the reveal is then lost: such a plugin must render the toolkit’s Sidebar. See ADR-0063.
  • The accessibility lane also checks the published sidebar (#200). Before, it measured only the drafts-on build, so the sidebar readers see was never checked. Now CI also serves example/dist-nodrafts to two more Playwright projects, published-light and published-dark, which run the sidebar specs. A new spec checks that draft entries appear only in the drafts-on sidebar and that previous and next links skip drafts in the published build. The server stops when the dist and the draft mode it was given disagree.
  • Every machine surface is compared across builds (#201). The sitemap, RSS feed, llms.txt files, api/ JSON, the OKF bundle and the Pagefind index must be byte-identical between two builds with the same draft setting. Between the drafts-on and drafts-off builds only the drafts’ own page records may differ. Each surface must match at least one file, so a renamed surface fails the check instead of dropping out.
  • The page chrome has an explicit target-size check (#202). Every link and button in the header, sidebar, rail and footer must be at least 24 by 24 CSS px, or meet the WCAG 2.2 spacing exception. It runs at 1280px and 1920px with the rail expanded and collapsed, and on a phone with the menu open.
  • The column on a page with a rail and no sidebar is checked to be centred (#199). Before, this was a code-review item. Now a Playwright spec measures it at each width, with the rail expanded and collapsed.
  • The stock-header fixture has a stamp, and pnpm fixture:stock-header recaptures it (#207). The fixture that the Header carrier is compared with is now captured from a build with the carrier switched off, so it is Starlight’s own header. stock-header.meta.json records the Starlight and Astro versions and the compressHTML setting it was captured with, and a fast test names the field that no longer matches and the command to run.

Changed

  • The toolkit sets Starlight markdown.processedDirs itself. Before, only src/content/docs got Starlight’s Markdown processing. Now the docs root is listed first, any directory you list under starlight.markdown.processedDirs follows, de-duplicated, and your other markdown options are merged in.
  • The scenarios API names its producer in generated_by (#182). Before, api/scenarios.json named its producer only as generated_from: "doc-kitty/gherkin", while the generated feature pages’ stamp says doc-kitty-gherkin/<version>. Now it carries generated_by: "doc-kitty-gherkin/<version>", an OKF tool actor matching that stamp. generated_from is removed in this same release (#183, see Breaking).
  • Metadata follows OKF v0.2 (#177). Before, updated was a date, okf_version sat only on the root index, and authors were email addresses. Now updated and stale_after take UTC timestamps (2026-10-18T09:30:00Z), every index declares okf_version: "0.2", and authors, generated.by and verified[].by use OKF actors (human:<id>, <tool>/<version>, process:<id>). Old forms still build, with a warning from the doc checks. Generated Gherkin and glossary pages name the tool and version that wrote them, and keep generated.at unchanged until their content changes. Date-times without a zone are now read as UTC; before they were read in the build machine’s local time, so such values may shift by its offset. Newly scaffolded pages carry a generated: stamp that records provenance only and grants no generated-page exemption. The metadata model documents how doc_status maps to OKF status.
  • The env reader honours vite.envDir and --mode, so drafts follow the files your build uses (#115). This affects sites that set vite.envDir or build with a custom mode. Before, DocKitty read .env* files only from the site directory and always used production (or development for astro dev), so DK_PUBLISH_DRAFTS in envDir, or in .env.staging, was ignored. Now a relative envDir is read from the site directory, envDir: false reads no files, and --mode staging reads .env.staging. The mode local is refused, as in Vite. The process environment still wins. The gates follow your config’s envDir; dockitty-assert-build-artifacts and dockitty-check-redirect-coverage without --docs stop when the config mentions envDir unless you pass --env-dir <dir|false>. Sites with neither setting are unchanged.
  • Heading anchor links stay off, as on 0.3.0 (#144). Starlight 0.34 and later add a link icon to every heading by default. The toolkit sets Starlight’s markdown.headingLinks: false, so headings, decks and the accessibility baselines look as they did. To turn the anchors on, pass starlight: { markdown: { headingLinks: true } } to defineDocKittyIntegrations.
  • The toolkit sets compressHTML: true, overriding your own setting (#145). Astro 7 defaults to compressHTML: 'jsx', which drops the whitespace between inline elements, so copied text and search excerpts read “status:activeUpdated”. The toolkit’s integration pins compressHTML: true, the pre-Astro-7 output, and it runs after your astro.config.mjs, so a compressHTML you set there has no effect. A configurable option may follow.
  • A build with broken docs pages stops at the first one (#119). Before, the build listed every docs page with invalid frontmatter in one run. Astro 7’s content sync stops at the first invalid entry, so you now see one page per run. Run dockitty-validate-frontmatter docs first to see them all at once. Render errors, such as a broken Gherkin fence, also stop the build at the first page, and the frontmatter check does not find them; the old “N Gherkin error(s) on M pages” summary is no longer printed.
  • RouteShapingOptions no longer has unpublishedDirs or unpublishedPaths; the withheld drafts now travel in a per-config build state. The type is an internal seam, not supported API.
  • Draft pages gain one p.dk-draft-notice in their HTML (#198). Pages that are not drafts are unchanged.
  • Existing @dk:context tags are now checked against the glossary (#197). Before, a tag naming a context the glossary does not define was silently ignored for disambiguation. Now the site build warns about it, even on a site that does not set defaultGlossaryContext. The warning never fails the build or changes a page.
  • Feature pages use the Specification layout by default. Before, kind: Specification fell back to the Default layout. Now it uses the new layout, so pages with tags or a source gain the card.
  • The example site maps its shipping and HR folders to glossary contexts. The three shipping features no longer carry @dk:context=shipping, and the HR page now resolves policy to the HR definition. The example also turns on the imperative-step lint, with zero warnings.
  • The column shift between pages with and without a rail is intended (#204). A page without a rail starts its column further along, by 144px from a 1600px viewport. Stock Starlight shifts too, and reserving a rail on every page was rejected. See Collapsible TOC rail.
  • The sidebar reveal script moved from head to the Sidebar carrier. It is now one inline script right after the sidebar markup, and the head entry is gone.

Fixed

  • Every RSS item has a <pubDate> (#190). Before, generated Gherkin feature pages and glossary pages, which carry no updated, were feed items with no date, so feed readers sorted them unpredictably. Now an item takes its date from updated, else from the page’s generated.at stamp, and the feed is ordered by that date. A page with neither is left out of the feed, with a build warning. A generated page without updated is dated by its generated.at, so it moves in the feed when the generator regenerates it.
  • Every page has exactly one <h1> (#191). Before, a page whose body started with # Title rendered two: Starlight’s title and the body heading. Now the first body H1 that repeats the frontmatter title is removed, wherever it sits, and links to its anchor still work. Any other body H1 becomes an H2, so the title stays the page’s only <h1>. Slide decks are unchanged. You do not need to edit your Markdown.
  • Shared links show a full card on Slack, WhatsApp and LinkedIn (#180). Before, the spec-kitty theme’s share image was an SVG, which those platforms do not show, and the card carried no image size or type. Now every page’s og:image is a 1200x630 PNG with og:image:width, og:image:height and og:image:type, and the site-wide card’s alt text is the site title. A page whose social_thumb or hero_image is an SVG gets the site-wide card, with a build warning. A theme whose assets.socialImage is an SVG gets the toolkit’s default card, with a warning to give it a PNG or JPEG.
  • Generated hub pages no longer appear as RSS items (#127). Before, the section and folder indexes the Gherkin generator writes, and the generated glossary index, showed up in rss.xml with no news of their own. Now generated hubs stay out of the feed; authored hubs are unchanged.
  • The home page’s address no longer redirects (#188). Before, the home page’s canonical URL, its og:url and its sitemap entry had no trailing slash (…/doc-kitty), and GitHub Pages answered that address with a 301. Now all three end in /. This reverses the 0.2.x choice of a slash-less root sitemap entry; every other page is unchanged.
  • Footer “Back to top” jumps to the top again (#187). Before, it linked #top, an anchor no page has. Now it links #_top.
  • llms.txt no longer has an empty heading (#189). Before, the root group was headed ## when the section registry had no root label. Now it is ## Overview.
  • astro dev shows the theme and the favicon on every request (#170). Before, a theme stylesheet request with a query such as ?inline rendered the page unthemed, and a site with a base got a 404 for its favicon at the path without the base. Built sites were never affected.
  • Glossary links on Markua pages match the build (#113). Before, the page’s “terms used” block re-read a Markua page without the Markua passes, so its links could differ from the page’s. Now it replays them when markua: true.
  • A second DocKitty config in the same process (for example a test suite) no longer inherits the first config’s draft-publication setting (#167). Before, defineDocKittyIntegrations left the first config’s internal environment values in place, so the second config read the first one’s setting. Now each config starts with those values cleared. Production builds, which define one config per process, were not affected.
  • The build gates now follow the envDir of an imported base config, and a broken config stops them (#173). Before, assert-build-artifacts and check-redirect-coverage searched the config’s text for envDir, so a value set in an imported base config went unseen and a comment could trigger a failure. Now assert-build-artifacts, check-redirect-coverage and check-links evaluate astro.config.* and honour the base config’s envDir. They exit 2 when the config will not evaluate, times out, or is not the config that decides the site root. --astro-config picks the config; --env-dir <dir|false> skips evaluation. An envDir set in an integration’s updateConfig hook, and configs that vary by build mode, are still not seen.
  • A retired generator stamp names the right regeneration step (#210). The frontmatter error for a retired glossary stamp pointed at the Gherkin generator. Now it names dockitty-generate-feature-pages for Gherkin pages and a site build for glossary pages.
  • The Markua showcase no longer requests a missing image (#194). Before, its web-image figure loaded https://example.com/mac.jpg, which does not exist. Now it loads the site’s own macintosh.svg by its absolute site URL, so it still shows web-URL passthrough. dockitty-assert-no-broken-links takes an opt-in --no-external-images (with --allow-image-host <host>) that fails a built <img> loaded from another host, or a same-site absolute image missing from the build, without fetching anything; the example’s pnpm assert:no-broken-links turns it on.
  • The sidebar no longer jumps on a first visit (#203). Before, the sidebar painted at the top and scrolled to the current entry only after the whole page had loaded, which took seconds on a slow link. Now the entry is in view at first paint, once the sidebar markup has arrived. In-session navigation still restores the position Starlight saved.
  • The header search starts where the column starts (#216). Before, it sat 24px before the column on a rail page and 168px off with the rail collapsed. Now it lines up with the column on pages with and without a rail, with the frame capped or not. A site title wider than the space before the column keeps the search after the title, as stock Starlight does.
  • The column no longer runs under the collapsed rail toggle (#217). From 1152 to 1296px with the rail collapsed, the column ran 7px under the toggle. Now, below 84rem (1344px), the pane’s end padding with the rail collapsed is the toggle’s width plus 4px.
  • The Persona card no longer leaves a large blank at wide widths (#206). --dk-width-passport now defaults to the metadata band’s width, 50rem instead of 32rem, and the card is start-aligned with the text below it. The card now follows --dk-width-band, so a site that sets --dk-width-band also resizes the card. A site can still set --dk-width-passport itself.
  • The OKF export no longer credits a human edit to the scaffold (#226). Before, the export took generated.by, at and content_hash from any generated stamp, so a page that began as a scaffold and was then rewritten was exported as generated by doc-kitty-scaffold. Now only an ownership stamp (doc-kitty-gherkin/<version> or doc-kitty-glossary/<version>) supplies them. For any other stamp, by is the first author, who leaves authors, else process:dockitty-export, and at is updated, else that stamp’s at. RSS still dates an item from updated, else generated.at, and the agent API is unchanged. See the ADR-0059 note.

Documentation

  • The site’s changelog shows every release, from CHANGELOG.md (#192). Before, the example site’s changelog was a hand-written page that stopped at v0.1.0. Now /changelog/releases/ renders the repository’s CHANGELOG.md at build time, so there is no copy to keep in sync, and pnpm assert:changelog fails when a ## [x.y.z] release is missing from the built page.
  • Install 0.4.0 from the site’s new install guide (#193). Before, the site had no install guide and Getting started showed repository-internal commands. Now /guides/install/ covers Node >=22.22.0, the astro 7, Starlight 0.42 and @astrojs/markdown-remark 7 peers, the GitHub Packages .npmrc setup and the first build, and links the 0.3 to 0.4 migration guide; Getting started points consumers there. A test keeps the guide’s Node floor, peer ranges, package name and wiring equal to src/package.json and the consumption-test fixture.
  • ADR-0061 and ADR-0062 record the decisions. The consumer setup guide, the authoring guide, the Gherkin architecture page and the theming page cover the new options, the tag, the layout and the notice.

Known limitations

  • Every build logs The collection "i18n" does not exist or is empty and one Could not render /presentations/<deck> from route /[...slug] warning per deck page (#144, spike B17). Both are harmless: Starlight 0.42 looks up an optional i18n collection that a site without translation files does not have, and Starlight’s catch-all route yields to the higher-priority /presentations/[...slug] deck route, which is the intended page. Defining an empty i18n collection only replaces the warning with another, and keeping deck pages out of Starlight’s route needs a change to how decks are collected, so both are left for a later release.
  • With a frame cap between 72rem and 84rem on a wider viewport, the column can still run under the collapsed rail toggle (#220). The 120rem default is not affected.
  • Above the 120rem cap, the sidebar’s tint starts at the frame edge while the header bar spans the viewport (#224, open design decision).
  • On a slow first paint, Starlight’s rail can be drawn next to the left sidebar and then jump into place (#223). The layout-shift check counts such partial-paint shifts and can flake under parallel load (#222); it runs in the light project only until it is redesigned.

0.3.0 — 2026-10-14

This release lets you write Gherkin scenarios in any page, shows their test results from your Cucumber report, rewrites relative Markdown links to working routes, widens the reading column to 60rem and makes sidebars stop repeating their own labels. You now set index names in one place, on defineDocKittyIntegrations, and the DocKitty commands read them from your site config. Several silent problems now stop the build with a message that names the file: two files at one address, a misspelt theme slot, empty Gherkin sources. Upgrading from 0.2.0: read the Breaking section first.

💥 Breaking

  • Remove --index-basename from your CI scripts: the DocKitty commands now read index names from astro.config.* (#136). Before, each command took its own index names, and dockitty-check-links accepted both README and index while the build used only README. Now dockitty-check-links, dockitty-validate-frontmatter, dockitty-check-redirect-coverage, dockitty-generate-feature-pages, dockitty-new-doc and dockitty-scaffold read your site config (about one extra second per run) and print the names they used. With no config next to the docs folder, they warn and use README; pass --astro-config <path> if your config lives elsewhere. A missing or broken config path exits 2. If you keep the flag, it must list the same names as the config (order and letter case aside), or the command exits 2.
  • Move indexBasename from docKittyDocsLoader to defineDocKittyIntegrations in astro.config.* (#136). Before, you could set index names on the integration, the loader and the command line, and they could disagree. Now the integration is the only place, and the loader takes the value from it. If the loader still sets a different value, the build stops and shows both. Once the names are on the integration, delete the loader option. See ADR-0050.
  • Keep one file per page address: two files served at the same address now stop the build (#135). Before, a folder with both README.md and index.md built with a warning, and page.md next to page.mdx, or two names that differ only in letter case, went unnoticed. Now the build, dockitty-check-links --strict (exit 1) and dockitty-validate-frontmatter stop and name the files, the address and a fix. Drafts count too, and so do case-only differences, because those files overwrite each other on macOS and Windows. Rename or remove all but one file in each group.
  • Generated glossary pages take your site’s index name, and the build stops in three new cases (#129). Before, the generator always wrote glossary/index.md. Now it uses index when your index names list it, and otherwise your first index name: on a site without index, glossary/index.md becomes glossary/README.md, and likewise for each context folder. If you commit generated pages, commit the rename. The build now stops, names the path and writes nothing when a file you wrote or a symbolic link sits where a generated page goes, when glossary/ or a context folder is a symbolic link, and when an index name is not a plain file name (one path segment, no leading ., no surrounding spaces), is empty, or is log.
  • On a site that sets gherkin: { sources }, ```gherkin fences and ::gherkin{…} lines change meaning (#120). Before, fences rendered as code blocks and a ::gherkin{…} line printed as text. Now fences render as structured scenarios, and ::gherkin{…} includes a .feature file from the folders in includeRoots (default: sources); an include whose file is outside them, missing or not a .feature file fails the build. Add raw to a fence (```gherkin raw) to keep it as code, or set fences: false to keep every authored page as it was. An unknown key in the gherkin option is now a config error instead of being ignored. Sites without the gherkin option are unaffected.
  • Regenerate your committed feature pages once (#120). Generated feature pages now show quoted step arguments as code (see Changed), so a regenerated page differs from the committed one. Run dockitty-generate-feature-pages once, or the --check gate reports the drift.
  • The build stops when no source yields a Gherkin feature and generated pages exist (#122). Before, a source folder that was not checked out, such as an uninitialised git submodule, made the build warn and delete every generated page. Now the build stops before writing anything and removes nothing. When you do want the pages removed, set gherkin.allowEmpty: true, or pass --allow-empty to dockitty-generate-feature-pages, for that one build. --check is unchanged.
  • Move pages you want published out of _meta/ (#138). Before, Markdown at any depth under a _meta/ folder, and files named _meta.md or _meta.mdx, were built and linked like any page. Now they are not published, and dockitty-check-links --strict skips them. The YAML registry files in _meta/ still load, and dockitty-validate-frontmatter still checks the Markdown there.
  • dockitty-new-doc --section and dockitty-scaffold create your first index name (#136). Before, a site with index names ['index', 'README'] could get a README.md. Now it gets index.md. An --index-basename value that is not one of your index names exits 2.
  • A theme slot name outside the dk: set stops the build (#114). Before, a misspelt slot such as dk:site-heading in a plain-JavaScript config was accepted, and the stock component rendered without a message. Now the config fails to load with an error that names the slot and lists the valid names. Correct the name. A theme typed as DocKittyTheme in TypeScript already caught this. See ADR-0052.
  • docKittyDocsLoader rejects a custom pattern (#133). Before, a narrowed pattern changed which pages were built but not which pages relative links could point to, so a .md link could be rewritten to a page that was never built. Now the loader throws when pattern is anything but the default. Leave pattern unset; to keep a file out of the site, move it out of the docs folder or name it log.md.
  • Rename any Gherkin file called index.feature (#137). Before, it was accepted unless your index names included index, and its generated page then collided with the folder’s landing page. Now the build stops on it whatever your index names are.

Changed

  • The reading column is wider, and all body content uses it (#154). The default --dk-width-content goes from 45rem (720px) to 60rem (960px), so prose, tables, diagrams, code blocks and components share one wider column instead of a narrow strip on large screens. The column still stays clear of the “On this page” rail and respects --dk-width-frame; phones and tablets look as before. Prose lines grow from about 92–101 to 123–135 characters. To keep the old width, set :root { --dk-width-content: 45rem; }. See Theming and chrome and ADR-0053.
  • Sidebars no longer repeat their own labels, on every site with autogenerated groups (#112). Before, a folder whose only page was its index showed as a group holding the same name (glossary contexts read hr > hr), and a section’s index repeated its heading (“Guides > Guides”). Now a nested one-page folder shows as that one link, in the folder’s place, and a section index whose label repeats its heading reads “Overview”, unless another page in the group already has that label. Top-level sections stay groups, and previous and next links keep the page title. “Overview” is English only for now (#161 tracks translating it).
  • Quoted step arguments render as code, on generated pages and in fences and includes alike (#120). A double-quoted argument such as "spec-kitty init --force" renders as inline code with its quotes, so the page no longer curls the quotes or turns -- into a dash, and the value copies exactly. This applies in data-table and Examples cells too. Text outside quotes is still typeset, and a quoted argument is no longer glossary-linked.
  • A broken in-page Gherkin fence or include fails the build (#120). Before, the page built empty. Now a Gherkin syntax error, or an include whose file, scenario or tag is not found, stops astro build with one [dk-gherkin] <page>:<line> error listing every broken page, and keeps failing until you fix it.
  • A Gherkin folder whose features are all drafts gets a draft hub (#124). Before, it got no hub, so with drafts built (the default) the sidebar asked for an index page you could not add. Now the generator writes a hub marked doc_status: draft with no list, built only when drafts are and linked from no published hub. The generated files do not depend on DK_PUBLISH_DRAFTS, so --check agrees in both modes. Such a folder gets one new generated file: run the generator once, or --check reports it as added.
  • A mis-cased @wip or @deprecated tag warns (#123). Before, a tag such as @WIP was published silently as an ordinary page tag. It still is, since the status shorthands match exactly as Cucumber tag filters do, but the build now asks “did you mean @wip?”.
  • dockitty-check-links checks reference-style link definitions and names a bad option (#131). Before, a dangling [label]: target line passed, and an unknown option was read as a docs folder that could not be opened. Now the definition is reported like an inline link, and an unknown option or the --name=value form stops the command before scanning, names the option and exits 2. The failure summary reads “N link problem(s) in M file(s); F file(s) scanned, C reference(s) checked.”

Added

  • Gherkin in any page (#120). Set gherkin: true and a ```gherkin fence on any docs page renders as a structured scenario: the feature and scenarios as headings in the page outline, steps as a list with the keyword in bold, data tables and Examples as tables, doc strings as code blocks, and # comments hidden. A fence may hold a whole feature, scenarios without a Feature: line, or bare steps. Inside a list, quote or aside the headings stay out of “On this page”. Slide decks keep fences as code, and generated feature pages are left as they are. See ADR-0051.
  • Include a .feature file from your repository with ::gherkin{src="…"} (#120). Include the whole file, one scenario with scenario="<exact name>", or the scenarios and Examples rows that carry any of tags="@a @b" (inherited tags count). Each include ends in a source line naming the file, linked with sourceUrlPrefix. Includes need gherkin.includeRoots (or sources) and read only regular files of at most 1 MiB inside those folders. A page that includes a file is re-rendered when the file changes, in a build and in the dev server.
  • New gherkin option forms (#120). gherkin: true turns on fences only, with no generated pages. The object form gains fences (default true) and includeRoots, and sources becomes optional: it is what turns on generated pages and the behaviour section.

0.2.0 — 2026-10-13

Read this before upgrading: set DK_PUBLISH_DRAFTS=off in the build that deploys your live site. This release adds that setting. Its default is on: draft pages are built and listed, as in 0.1.1, and are now also marked noindex and left out of site search. A page is a draft when its frontmatter says doc_status: draft or has no doc_status at all. A deployment that does not set off publishes its drafts as noindex pages:

Before you set off, give every live page a status other than draft, such as doc_status: active. A page with no doc_status counts as a draft, so off would leave it out of the build.

The version is 0.2.0 because the layout, sidebar and redirect-gate changes below are breaking, and under 0.x the minor number marks a breaking release.

💥 Breaking

Each item is described in full under Changed.

  • A theme that sets dk:site-header now replaces the stock header. The slot name was already valid in 0.1.1 but did nothing. Now the theme’s component replaces the header, including search and the theme select, so it has to supply them.
  • The redirect-coverage gate has new flags and a new failure. With drafts off it needs --docs and --declared-redirects to accept an old URL that leads to a draft, and it fails on any redirect stub that leads to a missing page.
  • Sidebar group labels and order change. Groups take their index page’s title and sidebar.order.
  • A page with no h2 or h3 loses its “On this page” rail.
  • The page frame is full width by default. Set --dk-width-frame for a capped frame.
  • The reading column is narrower between 1152px and 1344px viewports: 528px at 1152px (was 600px) and 656px at 1280px (was 664px).

What is new: each carries <meta name="robots" content="noindex"> and has no record in the search index. A site that never set doc_status builds the same pages as before, and every one of them except the root page is now noindex and unsearchable. Give a page a status other than draft (for example doc_status: active) to make it indexable and searchable again. The sitemap, feeds, llms.txt and the agent index never listed drafts and still do not. The site’s root page is never a draft and never noindex.

    The marker follows the page’s status, not the setting described under Added: a draft is noindex whenever it is rendered, also on a site that does not load its docs through docKittyDocsLoader.

  • This project’s example site publishes its Plans section and the footnotes showcase. /plans/, the two mission pages and /guides/markua-footnotes-showcase/ were drafts and are now doc_status: active; /plans/missions/ is a new index page. All five are in the sitemap, the feed, llms.txt, the agent index and site search (67 published pages, was 56: those five and the six generated behaviour pages). The published site is built with DK_PUBLISH_DRAFTS=off. That build leaves out the five remaining drafts (/adr/template/, /behaviour/shipping/track-consignment/, /context/audience/draft-persona/, /guides/markua-footnotes-malformed/, /presentations/draft-preview/), and every baselined old URL resolves on it, /plans/features/mission-alpha/ and /plans/features/mission-beta/ included.

  • The “On this page” rail has a fixed width, equal to the sidebar width (18rem by default), at every viewport from 72rem. The reading pane takes the rest of the frame; its column is at most 720px. Between 72rem and 84rem (1152-1344px) the reading column is narrower than before: 528px at 1152px (was 600px) and 656px at 1280px (was 664px). From 1600px it is 720px (was 552px).

  • Rail links meet the 24px target size, so a long outline is taller than before. A page that set tableOfContents: false to pass a target-size check can show its outline again.

  • The rail’s collapse toggle moved. Expanded, it is centred on the rail’s inner edge; collapsed, it sits at the frame’s end edge. In keyboard order it now comes directly before the outline links (before, it was reached after the page footer), and it names the region it controls (aria-controls="dk-toc-panel"). A reader’s stored collapse preference is kept.

  • Sidebar groups are labelled and ordered from their index pages. A nested folder’s group shows its index page’s title (or sidebar.label) instead of the folder name, sibling groups follow the index pages’ sidebar.order and then their labels, and each section’s index page is the first entry of its group. In every group, links come before sub-groups, so sidebar.order cannot place a page between two groups. Previous/next links follow the new order. A folder with no titled index page gets a readable label from its name and a [dk-sidebar] build notice. A sidebar you supply yourself is not touched, and your own starlight.routeMiddleware runs after the toolkit’s. See Authoring.

  • The current page’s sidebar entry is scrolled into view when a page loads.

  • A page with no h2 or h3 heading has no “On this page” rail. Its outline would hold one link, so the rail and its toggle are left out and the text uses the width (27 pages on the example site’s default build, 26 with DK_PUBLISH_DRAFTS=off; three of each are the generated behaviour hubs).

  • Desktop “On this page” links get a 24px minimum target (WCAG 2.5.8, axe target-size) — toc-rail.css now gives every desktop TOC link min-height: 24px (flex-centred). Starlight’s own links were about 23px tall, which a densely nested TOC (a generated feature page’s Rule → Scenario entries) fails. This applies to every site with a TOC, whether or not it uses the gherkin option, so visual baselines of pages with a TOC shift slightly; regenerate them with the “Update a11y baselines” workflow (update-a11y-baselines.yml).

  • The redirect-coverage gate reads the draft setting. With drafts off, pass dockitty-check-redirect-coverage the flags --docs <docs-dir> and --declared-redirects <map-file> so it can report an old URL that leads to a draft as unpublished instead of failing it; without them the failure message names the missing flag. It now also fails on any redirect stub in the output that leads to a missing page.

  • The gates resolve the draft setting the way the build does. dockitty-check-redirect-coverage and dockitty-check-links read DK_PUBLISH_DRAFTS from the process environment, then from the site’s env files, then fall back to on, and print one line with the value, its source, the site directory and the mode. --site-root <dir> names the site (default: the nearest directory with an Astro config above the checked directory, else the working directory) and --mode <mode> the env-file mode (default production).

Added

  • --dk-width-frame — a token that caps the page frame, for example :root { --dk-width-frame: 90rem; }. Default 100%; a length or a percentage. A capped frame is centred, and the sidebar, the header content and the rail sit at its edges. It is a registered property, so an invalid value behaves as 100%. Set it on :root. On a very wide screen the default leaves the sidebar and the rail far apart, so such a site may want a cap. See Cap the page width.

  • DK_PUBLISH_DRAFTS — on or off (default on), read from the process environment and then from the site’s env files (.env, .env.local, .env.<mode>, .env.<mode>.local; later wins; mode is development for astro dev and production otherwise). Any other value stops the build with a message naming the setting and the accepted values. Set off in the build that deploys your live site, in the deploy job’s environment or in a committed .env.production.

    With off, a draft page is not written, is not in any sidebar or the search index, and returns 404. If a redirect in your redirects config ends at a draft page, its stub is removed at the end of the build, the old URL returns 404 until the page is published, and the build warns once, naming each one. With on, drafts are built, listed and marked noindex; the build log says so, and when nothing set the value it adds how to turn drafts off. Filtering happens in docKittyDocsLoader; a site that loads its docs collection another way builds its drafts with off too and gets a warning at the end of the build. See Draft publication.

  • A theme can replace the site header through the dk:site-header slot. The component renders once inside Starlight’s <header class="header">, in place of the stock header. Starlight keeps the skip link and the mobile menu toggle; the theme supplies the site title, search, social icons, theme select and language select it still wants. A theme that sets no such slot gets the stock header, with unchanged markup. See Theme header and ADR-0044, which makes Header the fifth toolkit-owned carrier.

  • @spec-kitty/doc-toolkit/route-middleware — the package export the integration registers as Starlight route middleware. You do not import it yourself. The ./config export also gains routeShapingIntegration, draftPublicationIntegration, routeShapingSource, ROUTE_MIDDLEWARE, ROUTE_SHAPING_MODULE_ID and RouteShapingOptions, ./schema gains applyDraftPolicy, and the package root gains isDraftEntry.   • Gherkin .feature files can be published as documentation (ADR-0046). A new opt-in gherkin option on defineDocKittyIntegrations ({ sources, section?, sourceRoot?, sourceUrlPrefix? }) parses every .feature under sources once with @cucumber/gherkin and generates one kind: Specification page per feature, plus a hub per directory holding a published (non-draft) feature, into <docsDir>/<section>/ (default behaviour) when the build starts. The pages are ordinary collection files, so the sidebar, sitemap, RSS, llms.txt, the agent API and glossary auto-linking pick them up. Feature-level @dk:<key>=<value> tags map to frontmatter (glossary_context, doc_status, audience, related missions and ADRs, updated, glossary_autolink, agent.priority); @wip/@deprecated set the status and other tags pass through to tags. Output is deterministic (generated.at is a source content hash), only changed files are rewritten, and stale generated pages are pruned. These stop the build: an authored file in the generated section (a symlink counts, and so does a symlinked section folder); two features that would produce the same page; a feature whose file name produces log or an index name such as README; a syntax error or a missing source directory; and, for the scenario index below, a page whose .feature source is missing or has changed since generation. An index basename with a path separator or a leading dot is refused. A draft feature (@wip, @dk:status=draft) still gets its page but is never listed in a hub, and a directory holding only drafts gets no hub at all. A @dk:status the generator cannot use (a typo in the case, no value, or two tags that disagree) makes the page a draft and warns, so a page you meant to hide does not go live. The example site lists its feature pages in its RSS feed; a generated page has no date unless the feature carries @dk:updated=<date>. With the option unset the build output is unchanged apart from the TOC target-size CSS under Changed. See the consumer setup guide.

  • dockitty-generate-feature-pages — a new package binary (and @spec-kitty/doc-toolkit/scripts/generate-feature-pages.mjs) that regenerates the feature pages without a build, or with --check exits 1 listing every added, changed, stale or authored path, so CI can fail when committed pages drift from their .feature sources. 0.1.1 — 2026-10-10

The first published version, as @spec-kitty/doc-toolkit on the GitHub Packages npm registry (npm.pkg.github.com). 0.1.0 was tagged under the previous name (@commondocs-kitty/toolkit) and was never published to any registry, so 0.1.1 is the first installable release. The rename below is breaking only for anyone who built from a source checkout; no registry consumer exists under either name. Installing from GitHub Packages needs a GitHub token with read:packages — see consumer setup. (The heading date is the release-prep date; the releasing runbook has you update it to the tag date.)

💥 Breaking

  • The project is now DocKitty and the package is @spec-kitty/doc-toolkit (#105) — the toolkit was renamed from @commondocs-kitty/toolkit to @spec-kitty/doc-toolkit, and the product name from “Common Docs — Kitty Variation” to DocKitty. Adopters must update their dependency and every @commondocs-kitty/toolkit/* import to @spec-kitty/doc-toolkit/* (the subpath exports are otherwise unchanged). The package has not been published to any registry, so there are no released consumers to migrate. Publishing under the @spec-kitty scope refines the zero-Spec-Kitty-coupling invariant (NFR-001): the toolkit still carries no Spec Kitty runtime coupling, but its own self-reference is no longer treated as coupling — see ADR-0043. The agent-API’s generatedFrom field in /api/index.json also changed from common-docs-kitty to doc-kitty; an agent that branched on the old value should update (the payload version stays 2, as the shape is unchanged).

A read-only verify job fails closed unless the tag equals src/package.json version, the tagged commit is on main, and the CHANGELOG has a section for it. It re-runs typecheck, lint, unit tests, and the clean-room consumption test with its self-test, then packs the tarball. A separate publish job — the only one with packages: write — installs nothing and publishes that tarball with the run’s built-in GITHUB_TOKEN, so no external publish secret is needed. Prerelease versions publish under the next dist-tag. A manual dispatch is a dry-run rehearsal and never publishes, even on a tag ref. The runbook is docs/ops/releasing.md.

The scripts are also exported as @spec-kitty/doc-toolkit/scripts/*.
  • Attribution for the upstream Common Docs specification (#105) — DocKitty is based on the Common Docs convention created by Christopher Skene. A new root NOTICE reproduces the upstream MIT notice (spec v1.2, © Christopher Skene) and ships inside the package; the README gains an Accreditation section, and the convention doc credits the Common Docs specification to Christopher Skene alongside the DocKitty variation.

A consumer can now author a single optional charter, resolved natively by doc-kitty with no Spec Kitty runtime dependency, under a documented per-axis default → consumer precedence. Existing _meta/*.yaml files are still honored (with a one-shot deprecation notice), so current consumers keep working unchanged; a charter-only consumer is now governed end-to-end — the frontmatter gate and every build output (llms.txt, the agent-API, rss.xml, the Hub grid, and the sidebar/sitemap) resolve through the charter. doc_status is extend-only (the canonical statuses stay reserved) and the required-field set keeps a non-removable title floor; a malformed charter fails closed.
